summary: Bacalhao Island light (1894), Notre Dame Bay: iron tower ordered for Western Bay Head, Conception Bay, then sent here; lit 6 Dec 1894; rotating keepers from early 1960s; heritage 1989; active.

lens.note: Upgraded from sixth order to fourth order in 1924 (Lighthouse Friends). Original 1894 light was a Trotter-Lindberg system with a flash every three seconds

structures.note: Prefabricated iron tower by Chance Bros. and Co., Birmingham (heritage statement). Focal plane 108.8 m in 1894 per Lighthouse Friends; 106.0 m in the 2026 Coast Guard list

structures.name: Bacalhao Island Sector Light
structures.note: Sector light established 2006 on a square skeleton tower near the lighthouse, replacing a pair of range lights (Lighthouse Friends; Coast Guard list H0635)
Keeper's dwelling 23 m from the tower, joined by a covered passageway (Lighthouse Friends). Original dwelling removed after 1966; a new dwelling was built in the early 1960s
Fog-alarm building built early 1960s after shipping companies requested one in 1961 (Lighthouse Friends)

staffing.note: Four keepers worked on a rotational basis after the early 1960s (Lighthouse Friends)

access.note: Grounds open, tower closed; best viewed by boat or from the air (Lighthouse Friends)

events.note: Iron tower ordered from Victoria Works for Western Bay Head, Conception Bay; the following year it went to Bacalhao Island instead
Tower and keeper's dwelling built; cast-iron tower by Chance Bros.
Placed in operation on 6 December 1894 by Keeper William Howell (Lighthouse Friends roster spells Holwell)
Lens upgraded from sixth order to fourth order
White flash every nine seconds with an acetylene gas light
Shipping companies requested a fog alarm in 1961; fog-alarm building built early 1960s
Original dwelling in poor condition; sold and removed from the island
Classified a Recognized Federal Heritage Building
Bacalhao Island Sector Light established on a square skeleton tower near the lighthouse, replacing a pair of range lights

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record and Lighthouse Friends say the light is active; the Coast Guard list (2026) gives a year-round light. Rowlett lists it as inactive (record conflict). Active is kept on the strength of the 2026 list and Lighthouse Friends.
Lighthouse Friends gives a 1894 focal plane of 108.8 m; the 2026 Coast Guard list gives 106.0 m. The record keeps the current figure.

The 1988 heritage statement and Lighthouse Friends describe a cast-iron cylindrical tower with a spiral daymark. The 2026 Coast Guard list describes a square skeleton tower with a red and white rectangular daymark. The sources do not explain the difference.
Lighthouse Friends' roster spells the first keeper Holwell; its text gives Howell.

Lighthouse Friends gives 1989 for the Recognized Federal Heritage Building classification. The heritage statement (report 88-135) ends with a date stamp of 1991.11.19. The story keeps 1989 from Lighthouse Friends; a human should check the Federal Heritage Building Review Office date.

notes_for_editor: Fact-check 2026-10-27 (independent pass, 46 quotes found on the first run). Checked the story sentence by sentence against Lighthouse Friends, the Coast Guard list (modified 2026-06-23), the heritage statement (report 88-135) and the CRHP entry. Changes: removed 'small island' and 'above the sea' (no source); removed the boat-only access flag (Lighthouse Friends says best viewed by boat or from the air, which does not say the island is reachable only by boat); 'first ordered' and 'first night' brought back to the source's words; the plaque lens date is now Lighthouse Friends' suggestion, not a settled fact; the 2026 tower description and the heritage statement's description are both stated and left unresolved; nominal range is stated as nominal. Still open: no Newfoundland government source was read; the keeper spelling Holwell/Howell is unresolved. Barry Potter (1988-1992) appears only as Lighthouse Friends prints him. Thin on history: no Newfoundland government source was read. The Journal of the House of Assembly of Newfoundland (cited by Lighthouse Friends) would hold the 1893-1894 tower order and the first keeper's appointment, but the Memorial University digital collection could not be reached from this environment (certificate verification error). A human or a later pass should check it. The keeper spelling Holwell/Howell is unresolved. The 2026 Coast Guard description (square skeleton tower, rectangular daymark) disagrees with the 1988 heritage statement (cast-iron cylindrical tower, spiral daymark); whether the tower was rebuilt is not known from these sources. Wikipedia says keepers and families lived on the island in 1911: that is a lead only and is not cited; a census or Newfoundland source would be needed. The lighthouses.wiki and nllh3d pages were read as leads only. Focal height 106.0 m (CCG) vs 108.8 m (LF 1894).
